text:
Eli (infra): FYI were seeing a localized p99 spike in us-west3 rack-19 since 05:12 UTC. Signs point to a large shuffle job causing NIC queue saturation.
Nina (sre): yep noticed it in the latency heatmap. Affected slices are a mix of dedicated and soft-affinity. Any hot tenants?
alloc-bot: [telemetry] rack-19 egress queue depth +310% between 05:12-05:28 UTC; packet drops = 6% (dash: https://telemetry.redwood/egress/1766665432).
Eli (infra): root cause appears to be a tenant launching 40 concurrent embedding workers from the same slice (tenant:blue-hill). This is stomping host egress and causing slab evictions.
Omar (platform): we should avoid evicting paid dedicated slices. Proposal: apply a short QoS cap on that slice and redirect non-urgent job prefixes to preemptible-cold.
Tess (product): quick heads-up: blue-hill has a reserved dedicated pool for their prod API. We mustn't touch prod traffic. Only background jobs.
Eli (infra): plan: 1) identify job prefixes (`jobs/emb-large`) 2) add routing rule to preemptible-cold for those prefixes 3) set temporary qos `max-egress=180mbps` for slice with TTL 20m.
Nina (sre): add a canary first: route one host's jobs for 5m then scale. Watch p99, retransmits, and kv-rehydrate-rate.
Omar (platform): routerctl commands (dry-run):
```
routerctl prefix add --tenant=blue-hill --prefix=jobs/emb-large --target=preemptible-cold --dry-run
qosctl set --tenant=blue-hill --max-egress=180mbps --tag=egress-contain --ttl=20m --dry-run
```
infra-oncall: running dry-run now. Also enabling annotation `notify:sales-eng` so account team is aware.
alloc-bot: [action] dry-run looks good. Pending apply.
Tess (product): I'll ping their TAM with the mitigation plan and request they pause any sweep runs for 30m.
Eli (infra): applying changes now (non-dry-run) in 2m. Nina please watch slab eviction rate and NVLink errors.
Nina (sre): watching. Initial signs: p95 restored to baseline within 90s post-change, p99 improving. No NVLink errors so far.
Omar (platform): after stabilization we should implement per-job egress budgeting and a console flag highlighting heavy batch jobs that can be offloaded. Filing ticket PLAT-9002.
infra-oncall: QoS applied at 2025-11-28T05:18:12Z (id: q-1766665432). Prefix routing enforced.
Eli (infra): summary: containment worked, 10% packet drops -> 0.8%, KV miss-rate fell 60%. Will follow up with a short incident note and recommend per-job metering.
Tess (product): thanks team. I'll coordinate a post-mortem with account team to keep the customer happy.
Nina (sre): :white_check_mark: closing loop unless we see recurrence.
